title: BlueFenix Health Renewal & Multi-Region Uplift Checkpoint
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on planned capacity uplift, adding EU region and pilot for private VPC. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for stable latency but wants dedicated + VPC proof points and SOC2 docs. Agreed next steps: internal benchmark run, security bundle share, draft amendment for add-on capacity.
topics: Current usage profile and growth forecast
Latency targets and dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs
Private VPC pilot and SOC2/compliance requests
Contract amendment and pricing next steps
next_steps: Ravi to run 48-hour throughput benchmark with customer prompt set (start 2027-05-03)
Maya to send draft amendment and uplift pricing by 2027-05-05
Noah to share SOC 2 Type II summary and audit point list by 2027-05-04
Customer to confirm internal stakeholders and target go-live date for EU on 2027-05-10 meeting
action_items: Ravi Patel - run benchmark with customer's eval prompts and share results - due 2027-05-06
Maya Chen - prepare amendment and pricing for 6-month top-up + EU add-on - due 2027-05-05
Noah Green - send SOC2/ISO docs excerpt and data retention policy - due 2027-05-04
Priya Singh - provide sample traffic profile and KV cache hit rates - due 2027-05-03
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2027-04-29 09:00 PDT | Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Green (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (BlueFenix Head of MLOps), Tom Baker (CTO), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Oliver Yang (Security)

Summary: quick renewal check, primary ask is capacity uplift and activation of EU region, plus a short Private/VPC pilot for PHI workloads. Security questions around retention, KMS and SOC2.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:08] Tom Baker: hey, tom here.
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: lena, hi.
[00:11] Priya Singh: priya on the call.
[00:13] Oliver Yang: oliver here.
[00:15] Maya Chen: great, ravi from our side and noah our csm, i'll hand to ravi to walk through the plan and benchmark ask.
[00:22] Ravi Patel: cool, thanks maya. so we've reviewed your usage trend, looks like 42% q/q token growth for the last two quarters, peak concurrency around 220 steady concurrent streams. you're currently on Hosted and a small reserved block, correct?
[00:34] Lena Ortiz: yes, hosted plus a 2-gpu reserved pool for high priority inference. the problem is when we run nightly batch rerank we hit higher tail latency, and the app SLA wants p95 under 300ms for interactive.
[00:46] Ravi Patel: right, that's the typical tradeoff. Dedicated capacity will give steady throughput and tail latency but adds cost. we talked about hybrid routing last time — route interactive to dedicated, fallback to hosted during maintenance.
[00:59] Tom Baker: what's the expected latency delta if we move interactive to Dedicated? are we talking 50ms improvement or more?
[01:06] Ravi Patel: based on similar customers, p95 can drop from ~600ms to ~220-280ms depending on model and seq length. for your mix (mostly 512 tokens), i'd estimate ~230ms once the KV cache warms. note: kv cache was sometimes transcribed as kv cash in our notes :)
[01:24] Priya Singh: and what about cost, we need an apples-to-apples number vs hosted. last renewal they raised the hosted unit price so we're sensitive.
[01:32] Maya Chen: yes we'll include a side-by-side. the optimize suggestions typically show x% savings with batching and prefix caching, but Dedicated baseline includes reserved GPU cost. we'll send a modeled TCO.
[01:44] Lena Ortiz: key ask — we need EU region for data residency and lower latency for EU clinicians. timeline is tight, want EU in prod by late June. can you hit that?
[01:55] Ravi Patel: June is tight but doable. two paths: 1) provision Dedicated in our EU region (fastest), or 2) spin up Private/VPC pilot in your EU account (longer, depends on your infra team).
[02:08] Oliver Yang: security-wise, PHI flows are the concern. Private VPC with customer-managed KMS is ideal. we need proof of invoice, audit trails, and how log retention works.
[02:19] Noah Green: we can share our SOC2 Type II report excerpt and our data retention policy. also the console has token-level logs and per-route tracing — we can configure longer retention with an add-on.
[02:34] Tom Baker: can i ask about encryption at rest for dedicated? we need HSM/KMS integration.
[02:39] Ravi Patel: yes Dedicated and Private both support KMS integration. Private allows your HSM-based key via our private control plane. Dedicated supports customer-managed keys through our KMS connector, though HSM-on-prem has additional steps.
[02:53] Priya Singh: how disruptive is switching from Hosted to Dedicated — downtime?
[02:58] Ravi Patel: almost zero for traffic if you do a canary rollout: start with a small percentage to Dedicated, run smoke tests, then ramp. it's in the console as a rollout plan. there can be short warm-up latency as caches fill.
[03:14] Lena Ortiz: ok, so the asks we have are: capacity uplift for peak of 350 concurrent, EU activation by end of June, and Private pilot for PHI in parallel.
[03:24] Maya Chen: got it. we should validate the 350 concurrency number with your traffic profile — priya, can you share the 24-hr peak window and token distribution?
[03:33] Priya Singh: yes i'll export the numbers, but quick note — our batch reranks spike tokenization up to 3x of baseline, so batching config matters.
[03:42] Ravi Patel: we'll include optimized batch profiles and an expected cost delta for your batch vs interactive mix.
[03:48] [04:00] --- demo / technical details ---
[04:01] Ravi Patel: for the benchmark i propose we run a 48-hour realistic workload: your prompt set, your seq length distribution, and concurrency ramp. we'll run on a Dedicated staging pool and capture p50/p95/p99 latency and KV cache hit rates.
[04:17] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. do you need access to our test credentials or just the prompt set?
[04:21] Ravi Patel: prompt set and a small signed API key for throttled traffic is easiest. we can run isolated load from our staging and share full logs.
[04:30] Tom Baker: what about multi-region failover — if eu goes down do we route to us-west? concern for clinicians in EU.
[04:38] Noah Green: yes smart routing allows region policies. you can set primary eu with fallback to us-west. we also support automatic fallback to smaller model variants to preserve availability.
[04:48] Priya Singh: are model variants automatically compatible? like quantized variants?
[04:52] Ravi Patel: they are, we keep model flavor compatibility, but you should validate quality via a short eval. there can be small output variance with quantization.
[05:00] Oliver Yang: circling back to compliance — we need to review your audit logging retention and encryption key lifecycle. any SLA on log delivery?
[05:09] Noah Green: logs are available via the console and exportable to your SIEM. retention default is 30 days; extended is available as an add-on to 365+ for audit purposes. key rotation is supported and we can provide rotation logs.
[05:25] [05:45] customer side discussions (inaudible background)
[05:48] Lena Ortiz: also can you include a cost estimate for a staged approach: month 1 go-live small eu pool, month 2 bump to full capacity.
[05:58] Maya Chen: yes will send staged pricing with a commitment ladder.
[06:03] Tom Baker: one more — procurement will want a redline of the SOW amendment for the uplift. can you provide an initial draft?
[06:09] Maya Chen: yes i'll do a draft amendment for 6 months with an option to extend.
[06:14] Ravi Patel: technical note: for the 350 concurrency, we'll recommend a Dedicated pool of 6 x L40 or equivalent (estimate) but we'll refine after the benchmark.
[06:25] Priya Singh: L40? we currently use gpus with different names, will you map to our cloud sku?
[06:30] Ravi Patel: yes we map to cloud SKUs in the proposal. sometimes the model/kernel perf varies a bit by hw; we'll include that in the benchmark report.
[06:40] [07:00] --- security clarifications ---
[07:01] Oliver Yang: about data residency — for Private VPC, is metadata ever staged in US region? we need clear lines.
[07:07] Noah Green: with Private VPC, control plane can be in-region and data plane stays in your VPC; we can provide an architecture diagram. if you go Dedicated hosted we persist logs in the region you choose, but cross-region metadata may still be processed for control operations — we'll clarify specifics in the security bundle.
[07:25] Oliver Yang: ok please add that to the docs.
[07:29] Lena Ortiz: and we need an explicit retention policy for transcripts and a delete process for cached KV entries holding PHI.
[07:38] Ravi Patel: we support manual and automated cache purge, and we can set TTLs on KV caches for sensitive routes. we'll include operational runbook steps in the pilot docs.
[07:49] [08:10] --- commercial / contract discussion ---
[08:11] Maya Chen: pricing approach: base renewal for current capacity plus a 6-month uplift add-on for Dedicated + EU region. we can do a short-term uplift (monthly) or commit for a discount. preference?
[08:23] Tom Baker: procurement favors a 6-month commit if there's a predictable discount. but legal needs the amendment.
[08:30] Maya Chen: understood. i'll draft the amendment and include both committed and month-to-month legs.
[08:36] Lena Ortiz: do you have a pilot credit or trial for the Dedicated benchmark?
[08:40] Maya Chen: we can offer a one-time benchmarking credit to cover part of the Dedicated staging run. i'll note that as a pilot credit in the draft.
[08:49] Ravi Patel: tech detail: we recommend enabling prefix caching and route-level batching for your rerank job to reduce cost. we can tune batch window so interactive stays snappy.
[08:59] Priya Singh: re: routing, if we enable batching for rerank will that impact latencies for interactive routes?
[09:05] Ravi Patel: no — batching is per-route, so interactive route remains low-latency, batch route is configured separately. just be mindful of tokenization overhead.
[09:14] [09:30] --- Q&A and clarifications ---
[09:31] Tom Baker: who will be our main contact during the pilot?
[09:34] Maya Chen: primary contact will be noah for operational, ravi for tech, and me for commercial.
[09:40] Lena Ortiz: ok that's clear.
[09:42] [10:00] --- Recap ---
[10:01] Maya Chen: recap: 1) run 48-hr benchmark on Dedicated staging with customer's prompt set (ravi), 2) draft amendment with staged pricing (maya), 3) SOC2 docs and retention policy (noah), 4) customer to share traffic profile and prompts (priya).
[10:20] Lena Ortiz: looks right. target mid-june for initial eu smoke, prod by late june if benchmarks pass.
[10:29] Maya Chen: we'll aim for the timeline; next meeting tentatively 2027-05-10 to review benchmark and pricing.
[10:35] Tom Baker: i'll get procurement and legal in that next meeting.
[10:38] Oliver Yang: we'll want a short security call after you share the bundle.
[10:42] Maya Chen: yes we'll schedule a 30-min security deep dive.
[10:45] [11:00] Closing pleasantries and meeting ends.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional background noise and some words auto-misparsed (L40 vs L4O, KV cache as KV cash) — please refer to recordings for detail.

Referenced artifacts/links:
- draft amendment template (will be attached by Maya)
- SOC2 excerpt (Noah to share)
- benchmark plan doc (Ravi to share link)
- prompt set & traffic export (provided by Priya via secure link)

End of transcript.
